evidence:
Scope and authority: I inspected the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl, not workbook-content.json. Quality Checks!A33:E33 says: "Each criterion is a concrete, browser-observable outcome with durable evidence and distinctive probes. Reports every instance." Internal Quality Checks row 33 repeats that wording; the remaining cells and comments in that row are empty, so there is no additional internal annotation to substitute for the shipped profile. I applied harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md, references/quality-checks.md:134-136, the browser-only contract in references/staged-task-contract.md:prompt.md and app_context.md, relevant deterministic reference recipes (rubric schema/prompt, independent outcomes, distinctive probes), and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, especially browser-only evidence and independent credit.

Inventory and completeness: Parsed and read all five judge.toml files and all five associated prompts, plus instruction.md, tests/app_context.md, all six public notes and seed_data.json. There are 79 criteria: Render 1, Constraints 1, Functional 64, Polish 7, Visual 6. All 64 functional descriptions point to the complete shared protocols in their injected prompt; judging those descriptions in isolation would miss their actual probes. No criterion requires reading submitted implementation, inferring a database engine, or awarding credit merely from a response schema. Functional prompt.md:7 explicitly says "Reading that source does not prove execution" and bars implementation files, bundles and database bytes; :13 requires actual values, markers, identities, revisions, messages and elapsed times. App_context.md:Evidence failures distinguishes missing tool evidence from observed product failure and forbids inventing a pass.

Gate outcomes: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires a newly chosen marker in both actual preview and console after ordinary Run, and says source text or a hardcoded sample is insufficient. tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 requires a real UI save, observed successful server exchange, independent clean-context loading, reload and matching identity/title/filename/exact source. It explicitly accepts server-rendered documents without a separate JSON endpoint and states that a toast, health response, static seed or localStorage alone is insufficient. These are state-changing, distinctive browser probes with retained records.

Functional outcomes, all groups: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:S01 (119-122) tests initial output, authored example execution and a separately saved exact copy; S02 (128-149) uses distinct JS/HTML DOM/log markers, a styled prior document, an actually working handler and a matching timer before CSS replacement; S03-S04 (156-182) observe delayed interaction markers, genuine pending timers, supersession/Stop, current success and recovery; S05/S07 (188-208) combine working own-document controls with blocked operation results, unchanged host state and transport delivery counts; S08-S13 (214-341) use concrete refusal/error markers, exact entered source line numbers, known successful renders and independent recovery; S14-S19 (347-391) observe ordered levels, expandable values, appended/cleared history, duration comparisons, timed authored edits and populated editor appearance; S21-S24 (397-436) freshly read complete saved records/revisions across loading, reload, one process restart, two actual dirty editors, title trials and successful controls; S34/S36 (442-456) preserve recorded draft/preview/console through two actual theme changes and distinguish nested callback completion from a shared timeout using durable log/DOM markers. No per-row full credit requires knowing hidden implementation state. The recipes constrain timing to actual browser actions, not time between model responses (:15, :113, :446).

Most indirect claims remain bounded and decidable: functional judge.toml:469 says the save/load canary measures "no observable execution side effect on its dedicated monitor record" and "is not proof that all server evaluation is absent." Protocol S21:401-403 records a matching successful write, checks the monitor after carrier create/update/load, waits five seconds before the final matching control and distinguishes browser requests. S07:204-208 checks two locally fulfilled nonce URLs with working fetch/Image controls, delivery counts, visible refusal and recovery; it explicitly rejects failed DNS/CORS/transport as proof. S23:421-425 demands real dirty editors and retained exact fields; an API replay alone cannot prove editor recovery. These limits avoid pretending a browser exchange can prove an internal architecture or universal absence claim.

Polish/Visual: polish judge.toml:23,32,41,50,59,68,77 names concrete usable surfaces, enabled controls, accessible labels, actual keyboard traversal, visible focus, recognizable loaded content and feedback. Its prompt.md:43-49 supplies the route and separates the recorded observations. Visual judge.toml:24-104 anchors each of the six criteria to rendered typography, contrast, spacing, hierarchy, consistency or cross-viewport composition; visual prompt.md:35-44 requires the named surfaces, both offered themes and the mobile comparison, with evidence for each score. The familiar qualitative visual anchors are allowed by the shipped Likert profile; they do not assert unseen source properties or a preferred design. Screens/DOM remain available as evidence of those states.

Counterexample analysis (textual, not newly executed variants): A conforming SSR implementation with observed HTML record data, native/composite keyboard menus, conflict prevention before submission, and static rollback snapshots remains eligible under constraints judge.toml:27, polish prompt.md:43-47, functional prompt.md:21 and :17. No false-fail witness survives those explicit allowances. A broken app with only hardcoded sample output, a fake Save toast backed only by browser storage, dead timers or API-only stale rejection cannot satisfy the authored marker, independent context, matching successful callback and real dirty-editor readbacks. These are useful attempted false-pass witnesses, but the written bars reject them; I found no credible residual instance for this row.

Raw evidence corroboration and limits: I independently verified the supplied RESULTS.json SHA256 ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09 against raw-evidence-index.json, verified current functional judge/prompt bytes against the recorded hashes, and checked all 22 recorded golden app hashes against frozen solution/app (zero mismatches). I inspected raw facts rather than treating the aggregate passed flag as evidence: facts.S07 records its control text, image width 2, baseline 2 deliveries and separate visible fetch/image refusal with final deliveries still 2; facts.S21 records monitor revision 3 unchanged after create/update/load/settled, no browser requests before control, then matching control success and revision 4; facts.S23 records exact retained dirty title/filename/source and fresh recovery revisions in both editor directions; facts.S05 records four blocked markers and unchanged storage; facts.S36 records nested-control-done, late-callback-entered, time-limit feedback, no forbidden completion, retained control and recovery. I cross-checked the implemented observations in drivers/boundary_flow.cjs:24-35, repair_flow.cjs:13-30, runtime_flow.cjs:80-84 and current_flow.cjs:49-56. These are scripted browser observations, not configured LLM judge measurements. No full configured verifier, Oracle score, target-builder result or measured judge workload is claimed. Check 32 passes as a complete criterion/protocol source assessment with partial runtime corroboration; this does not clear other QC rows.
